title: Name only existing files and live CLI verbs in a convention node's operative prose

facts.note: Convention node files are identifiable by kind/location in the toolkit checkout. Every existing node is in scope on every validation run, edited or not.
Produced by the existing validator test_convention_remedies_are_followable over ALL convention nodes in the toolkit checkout, including unchanged nodes and findings unrelated to the current plan.

values: operative prose added or edited (fix_hint, operational_guidance, normative_text, statement, term text, notes, description) naming a repo path or a CLI verb
facts.note: Additional trigger, not a prerequisite. Needs a diff-level observer that extracts path tokens and CLI verbs from operative-prose fields only, excluding provenance and examples/values blocks.
Additional trigger, not a prerequisite: a plan that renames/removes a file or verb should re-check every convention node quoting it.

fires: A validation run in the toolkit checkout finds an existing, unchanged convention node whose fix_hint names a file that does not exist — even if the current plan never touched that node.
A convention node's operative prose still instructs a CLI verb that has been removed from the toolkit.
A planner writes or edits a fix_hint naming a validator path that does not exist in the checkout.
A plan renames a validator or removes a CLI verb while convention nodes still quote the old spelling.
doesNotFire: The path appears only in provenance (`source.legacy_path`).
The path appears in an `examples`/`values` block as an illustration.
The path is a segment position in a schematic formula, an explicitly excluded mechanism, a conditional reference, gitignored runtime state, or is described in past tense as retired.
The run is in a consumer repo rather than the ATDD toolkit source repo (rule is platform-gated).

given: Any convention node in the toolkit checkout — existing and unchanged, or one you author/edit — whose operative prose (fix_hint, operational_guidance, normative_text, statement, term text, notes, description) names a repo path or CLI verb
when: the checkout is validated; also when you write such a node or plan to rename/remove a file or retire a verb it quotes
then: Every path named in operative prose must exist in the checkout and every CLI verb named must still resolve — a fix_hint is an executable promise.
prefer: Absent path: correct it to the real location, or drop the pointer if the thing no longer exists.
Retired verb: replace it with its live replacement (e.g. `atdd issue <N> --status <PHASE>` → `atdd coach transition <N> <PHASE>`; `atdd issue open` → `atdd coach issues open`).
When retiring a verb, record it with its live replacement.
When a plan renames a file or removes a verb, include updating every node that quotes it.
avoid: Half-repairs: swapping an absent path for one that is merely plausible — that produced this defect.
A remedy saying only "that verb is gone" without the live verb — itself unfollowable.
Describing a retired path in present tense — a defect, not a record.
unless: Provenance (`source.legacy_path` + `legacy_sha`) — pointing at a deleted file is what provenance is.
Illustrative paths in `examples`/`values` blocks — fictional by design.
Schematic `Formula:` templates — segments are positions, not directories.
A path named as an EXCLUDED mechanism ("no X") — a statement of absence.
A conditional reference ("if it exists", "when present").
A path the node declares RETIRED in past tense — a historical record.
why: A fix_hint is read exactly when the reader is blocked; a missing file or dead verb sends them nowhere. Historically nothing read fix_hints, so a verb removal and a validator rename left every quoting hint stale.
evidence: Each path token in operative prose resolves in the checkout, or falls under an authored exception.
Each CLI verb in operative prose resolves; retired verbs appear only with their live replacement or in past-tense records.
verifier_detail: Operative prose fields scanned: `fix_hint`, `operational_guidance`, `normative_text`, `statement`, `text`, `notes`, `description` — strings a reader is expected to act on. Provenance (a record) and examples (illustrations) are excluded — only operative prose makes a promise.

Unfollowable remedy = operative prose naming a repo path absent from the checkout, or a CLI verb that no longer resolves. The reader is sent nowhere at the exact moment they are blocked, which is when a fix_hint is the one part of a rule they read.

Retired verb = a CLI verb removed from the toolkit whose spelling survives in prose; each retired verb is recorded with the live verb that replaced it, because a remedy saying only "that verb is gone" is itself unfollowable. Known mapping: `atdd issue <N> --status <PHASE>` → `atdd coach transition <N> <PHASE>`; `atdd issue open` → `atdd coach issues open`.

Exclusions: `source.legacy_path` provenance (carries a `legacy_sha`; the monolith it names was deliberately deleted); `examples`/`values` blocks (a naming rule's negative example must NOT exist); schematic `Formula: ... -> contracts/theme/seg1/...` templates; paths named as excluded mechanisms ("no plan/_meta.yaml" — flagging would invert the node's meaning); conditional references ("if it exists", "when present" — predicate subject, not pointer); gitignored paths checked live via `git check-ignore` so the exclusion cannot outlive the path (the day it leaves `.gitignore` it stops being excused); paths declared retired — the test is tense, not the token ("#1270 retired the `.atdd/manifest.yaml` mirror" is a record; "the phase labels live under `.atdd/labels.yaml`" is a defect).

Runs against the checkout (all convention nodes, not only changed ones) and is `platform`-gated via `is_atdd_source_repo()`: in a consumer repo nodes arrive from the installed package while quoted paths are TOOLKIT-repo paths, so an ungated rule would flag nearly every path as absent in somebody else's repo (#272/#276). The installed package carries none of `plan/`, `docs/`, `.atdd/`, so it is not a resolvable root.

Disposition STRICT, severity 3; the disposition is the point. Calibration: naive scan found 179 of 332 paths absent; by cause 137 provenance, 34 illustrative, six real. Strict is affordable at six (unlike #1958 at 369-of-473 and #1943 at 101-of-229, which had to settle for advisory because the remedy was unaffordable), so this refuses instead of logging.
audit: schema_version 1.1.0; kind rule; status active; introduced_in 4.83.0.
Original name: "A convention node's remedy must be followable".
#1965: five remedies across four nodes were unfollowable — three named a file that is not there, two instructed `atdd issue`, removed in #1303 — and a sixth turned up while designing the rule.
Nothing read a fix_hint, so when the verb was removed and the smoke-acceptance validator renamed, every hint quoting them stayed exactly as written.
Same family as #1548, where the authorable exemplar carried a URN scheme retired by #1421 and following the documentation produced an invalid artifact.
Term ids/labels: operative_prose (Operative prose), unfollowable_remedy (Unfollowable remedy), retired_verb (Retired verb).

sharedNodes.text: strict: fails on every finding, no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline.
